why_chain.text: Wednesday 2026-10-07: CRWD fell 4.81% to $265.44. The model splits it into market -0.31, cybersecurity industry -2.15 (CIBR -1.44%) and company -2.35 points (z -1.53: bigger than a normal day, not extreme). PANW fell 3.42%.

The broad market fell as the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.365%, its highest since April 2002; tech came under pressure on worries that higher borrowing costs would limit the AI buildout, and CNBC named CrowdStrike and Palo Alto among the decliners.
why_chain.evidence: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/06/stock-market-today-live-updates.html (tier 2, read via search excerpt; page returned 403)

why_chain.text: No CrowdStrike-specific negative news was found: its two releases that day (IDC Leader recognition, CyberCert partnership) were minor positives, there was no 8-K, and the Motley Fool states 'there was no specific news'.

Why it fell more than its group: it was the most stretched name. Seven straight higher closes (+10.6%), a new intraday all-time high of $286.99 on Tuesday, 80% above its 200-day average, RSI 72, and 43.5x forward sales (above its own 2021 peak) and about 209x forward earnings. Stocks priced on profits far in the future lose the most when long-term interest rates jump, and holders with big gains take profits first.
why_chain.evidence: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/crowdstrike-stock-is-flying--but-the-valuation-math-is-sending-warning-signs-202714759.html (valuation figures, tier 3); data/metrics/2026-10-07.json; link between valuation and the bigger fall = inference (medium)

why_chain.text: Selling into strength had started on Tuesday: CRWD hit $286.99 (+5.3%) but closed at $278.86 (+2.27%), and its company part was already -1.03 that day despite positive news. Wednesday's volume was below average (0.84x the 20-day), which fits profit-taking more than news-driven selling.

Basic driver: higher long-term interest rates make distant profits worth less today, and CrowdStrike's price depends more than most on profits years away; this met a stock that had more than doubled this year. No published source gives a CrowdStrike-specific reason.

Tuesday 2026-10-06 (+2.27%) for contrast: software stocks hit 2026 highs as AI-disruption fears faded and earnings expectations rose (Reuters); Zscaler reaffirmed guidance at its investor day and called agentic AI its biggest opportunity ever; CIBR rose 2.0% and PANW/FTNT made record closes. CrowdStrike's own news (Fal.Con Europe sold out, StoneX target $325, startup accelerator) did not add a company-specific gain: the company part was -1.03.

products.name: Falcon AIDR (AI Detection and Response) and Falcon Guardian
products.what_it_is: CrowdStrike's product line for securing companies' use of AI; the release says Falcon Guardian 'secures AI agents at the point of execution' (general description beyond that sentence: tools that watch what AI assistants and AI agents are asked to do and what they do, and block attacks or data leaks, is background knowledge, not from the release).
products.analogy: A security guard who stands next to each AI assistant and checks every instruction it receives and every action it takes before letting it through.
products.buyers: Enterprises deploying AI assistants and AI agents (specific customers not disclosed).
products.how_it_works: Not described in the release beyond securing AI agents at the point of execution; sold as Falcon platform modules (subscription).
products.sales: not disclosed in dollars, ARR or customers. Company figure: 'AIDR business has grown more than 79-fold in three quarters since launch' (base not disclosed).
products.stage: Shipping (launched about three quarters ago per the release; exact launch date not verified)
products.size_for_company: Not computable: no revenue figure. Proxy: total ARR $5.84bn (Q2 FY2027); a 79-fold rise from an undisclosed base says nothing about its share of that.
products.competition: Palo Alto Networks, Zscaler and others market AI-security products (Zscaler's 2026-10-06 investor day pitched agentic AI as its biggest opportunity); AI labs' own security tools (e.g. Anthropic's Claude Code Security caused a CRWD selloff earlier in 2026 per a tier-3 report, date not verified).
products.why_investors_care: Thesis 2 says AI makes security more necessary; pillar 4 needs reported results from AI channels. This is a company-given growth figure, but not yet a dollar figure.
products.watch_next: Any AIDR ARR or customer count on the Q3 FY2027 call (early December, unconfirmed); Fal.Con Europe announcements 2-4 November.

products.name: Cybersecurity Startup Accelerator (with AWS and NVIDIA), fourth year
products.what_it_is: An eight-week program that helps young security companies build on CrowdStrike's Falcon platform.
products.analogy: Like an app-store maker running a school for app developers so more apps get built for its store.
products.buyers: Not a product; participants are early-stage security startups.
products.how_it_works: Startups get Falcon Foundry and Falcon API access, verified integrations and CrowdStrike Marketplace publishing; AWS adds marketplace onboarding, NVIDIA technical training; the Falcon Fund may invest.
products.price: not disclosed (no fee or investment amounts stated)
products.sales: none (ecosystem program); past cohorts: more than 90 startups that raised nearly $1bn
products.stage: Applications open to 2026-11-02; program 2027-01-11 to 2027-03-08; demo day RSAC 2027
products.why_investors_care: More third-party apps on Falcon can make the platform stickier; no near-term financial effect.
